hypotheses.reasoning: redis-cache restarted at 13:03:17 after node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it started with 0 keys (#157). Search-api's cache miss ratio jumped to 97% (baseline 5%) and then 94% (#158, #163), so nearly every search fell through to catalog-db. That load saturated catalog-db: connections 490/500 with CPU 99% (#162), and product lookups slowed to 4.4s (#164). search-api then hit its 5s query timeouts on products (#171, #202), and web-bff returned 504s (#172, #186, #198, #216, #230, #241). The trigger was a small cache restart, and the outage came from every miss hitting the database. Before 13:03 the cache hit rate was around 95% and latency was normal, so the cache loss is the onset. The 504s at web-bff are downstream symptoms and are described here rather than cited as root cause. Alternatives considered: the catalog-db slow queries are a consequence of the load rather than an independent fault (no lock or bad deploy seen); index-worker and catalog-svc show no errors.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore cache capacity: warm redis-cache (preload hot product keys from catalog-db or a replica snapshot) and enable persistence (RDB/AOF) so node replacements don't start empty. Temporarily throttle or rate-limit cache-miss reads to catalog-db, or serve stale or cached responses, to relieve connection and CPU pressure. Add request coalescing or a stampede lock on the miss path so concurrent misses for the same key collapse into one DB query. Then confirm catalog-db connections and latency return to baseline and the miss ratio falls.
